Read from the pooled analysis (PMID 33964925, BMC Pulm Med 2021): LEAP 1 randomised patients to INTRAVENOUS lefamulin 150 mg every 12 hours for 5-7 days with an OPTIONAL INTRAVENOUS-TO-ORAL SWITCH; LEAP 2 randomised to ORAL lefamulin 600 mg every 12 hours for 5 days. LEAP 1's comparator is moxifloxacin WITH OR WITHOUT LINEZOLID and LEAP 2's is moxifloxacin alone -- corroborated from the registered arm groups. This object's own question already states the comparator difference; THE ROUTE AND DURATION DIFFERENCE WAS NOT PREVIOUSLY RECORDED.

NOT that the pool is invalid -- an intravenous-to-oral switch and an oral course of the same drug are a defensible thing to combine, and the published analysis combines them. What is claimed is that a reader meeting one ratio should know the two arms differed in route, duration and comparator, and no field said so.

Methods. estimates were pooled under random-effects with the REML estimator; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials); and certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.2

Methods — synthesis

For early clinical response, a random-effects model was fitted with the REML estimator.1

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials) (), following . 2 result-level assessments were made. 2

A ceiling applies to every risk-of-bias judgement in this review; it is stated with the assessment itself rather than summarised here.3

Certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons., following . 0 pooled outcome(s) were rated. No domain is rated UP. Rating up for a large effect, a dose-response gradient or opposing plausible confounding applies to observational evidence; these are randomised trials, which start HIGH and can only be rated down. 1 outcome(s) were NOT rated because their pool is declined or withdrawn: there is no effect estimate to rate the certainty of, and rating one would be certainty about a number this review refused to publish.4

Results

The pooled risk ratio for early clinical response was 0.988 (0.953 to 1.02) across 2 trials, against moxifloxacin (with or without linezolid in LEAP 1).1

NOTED ON THIS POOL. CHECKED AND CLEAN. Read from the registrations on 2026-08-21: NCT02559310 registers 'Early Clinical Response (ECR)' (population: ECR); NCT02813694 registers 'Early Clinical Response (ECR)' (population: ECR). Both trials register the same primary in the same population, so this pool does NOT cross an analysis-population boundary. Recorded because a check that only speaks when it finds something cannot be told from a check that was never run. THE EXPERIMENTAL ARMS ARE NOT THE SAME INTERVENTION. Read from the pooled analysis (PMID 33964925, BMC Pulm Med 2021): LEAP 1 randomised patients to INTRAVENOUS lefamulin 150 mg every 12 hours for 5-7 days with an OPTIONAL INTRAVENOUS-TO-ORAL SWITCH; LEAP 2 randomised to ORAL lefamulin 600 mg every 12 hours for 5 days. THIS OBJECT POOLS THEM AS ONE INTERVENTION. LEAP 1's comparator is moxifloxacin WITH OR WITHOUT LINEZOLID and LEAP 2's is moxifloxacin alone -- corroborated from the registered arm groups. This object's own question already states the comparator difference; THE ROUTE AND DURATION DIFFERENCE WAS NOT PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. Whether these are non-inferiority designs is NOT established: the registration fields fetched do not use the word, and a pooled ratio from non-inferiority trials answers a different question from a superiority pool. Unresolved, not assumed. NOT that the pool is invalid -- an intravenous-to-oral switch and an oral course of the same drug are a defensible thing to combine, and the published analysis combines them. What is claimed is that a reader meeting one ratio should know the two arms differed in route, duration and comparator, and no field said so.2

The trials' results were closely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 0%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 0, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 0.731, on degrees of freedom 1.3

What this does not establish: NOT that either trial is free of bias -- NO RISK-OF-BIAS ASSESSMENT IS RECORDED, and a pooled estimate without one is an arithmetic result, not a graded finding. NOT non-inferiority or superiority: both trials were designed as non-inferiority studies against an active comparator, and a risk ratio near 1 with an interval spanning 1 is the EXPECTED result of a successful non-inferiority trial rather than evidence of no difference. NOT that the pooled interval is reliable at k=2 -- see the Hartung-Knapp interval, which is the honest width. NOT agreement with any published synthesis; none has been checked.4

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.5

Risk of bias in the included results

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials). The unit of assessment is a result1

A domain that cannot be judged from the sources READ is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect. Overall is capped at SOME_CONCERNS wherever a domain is NO_INFORMATION. 2

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT ASSESSMENT WAS OBTAINED FROM: GPT-5 Codex (openai family), via `codex exec`3

The assessment above was made by: Claude Opus 5 (anthropic family) -- the assessment above4

How the second assessor was asked: BLIND, from scripts/second_assessor_prompt.py, which assembles the prompt from an ALLOW-LIST of registry-sourced factual fields and REFUSES to send it if any RoB 2 verdict word appears in the assembled text. The second assessor was not shown this assessment and was not asked whether it agreed. It was given this project's NO_INFORMATION-never-LOW rule so the comparison measures judgement rather than house dialect.5

THE DISAGREEMENT RATE, reported as disagreement because agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing: 4 of 12 judgements -- 33.3%. Reported as DISAGREEMENT: agreement between two assessors given the same facts authenticates nothing.6

Certainty of the evidence

Certainty was rated with GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.. 1

No domain is rated UP. Rating up for a large effect, a dose-response gradient or opposing plausible confounding applies to observational evidence; these are randomised trials, which start HIGH and can only be rated down.2

LOW certainty. The two trials agree closely and the endpoint is the registered primary assessed under quadruple masking, so the downgrades are for unread deviation and missing-data domains and for k = 2, not for inconsistency or indirectness.3

Comparison with published syntheses

Published syntheses were identified as follows. PubMed E-utilities, executed 2026-08-21. Query, counts and per-record disposition in ssot/lefamulin-cabp-auto-full-review/appraisal/PUBLISHED_SYNTHESIS_SCREEN.json.1

This review was compared against 1 published synthesis(es); the denominator is stated because a comparison against an unstated number of reviews is not a comparison.2

What this comparison found. THE EXPERIMENTAL ARMS ARE NOT THE SAME INTERVENTION. Read from the pooled analysis (PMID 33964925, BMC Pulm Med 2021): LEAP 1 randomised patients to INTRAVENOUS lefamulin 150 mg every 12 hours for 5-7 days with an OPTIONAL INTRAVENOUS-TO-ORAL SWITCH; LEAP 2 randomised to ORAL lefamulin 600 mg every 12 hours for 5 days. THIS OBJECT POOLS THEM AS ONE INTERVENTION. LEAP 1's comparator is moxifloxacin WITH OR WITHOUT LINEZOLID and LEAP 2's is moxifloxacin alone -- corroborated from the registered arm groups. This object's own question already states the comparator difference; THE ROUTE AND DURATION DIFFERENCE WAS NOT PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. NOT that the pool is invalid -- an intravenous-to-oral switch and an oral course of the same drug are a defensible thing to combine, and the published analysis combines them. What is claimed is that a reader meeting one ratio should know the two arms differed in route, duration and comparator, and no field said so.3

On what basis their trial set is known: BOTH TRIALS NAMED IN THE ABSTRACT by their study names and their designs described. Registration ids are matched from this object, which keys LEAP 1 and LEAP 2 to those NCTs.4

No numeric comparison is made because the pooled ECR estimate was not extracted from the abstract -- recorded as not read.
